answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a real coastal beacon the keeper must tend in person: each keeper rows out to one named headland beacon, polishes its lamp, and logs the night's light in an umber-stamped logbook countersigned by the harbor master, while the yarrow planted beside the beacon proves the keeper walks the ground each week. One keeper cannot tend two beacons on the same stormy night, and the harbor license fee doubles per beacon on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real beacon, another weekly boat trip, another human, and twice the prior fee.
